author: microscope_agent

observable.name: tracer_brightness
observable.definition: The detected signal rate of one tracer under the illumination and exposure this card states, separated from background. Measured here because it cannot be asked for: it depends on this dye, this lot, this illumination and this camera together, so no vendor sheet and no prior run holds one.

targets.note: One decade is what unblocks A1. Its detection limit and SNR floor compare a per-particle rate against read noise and background, and those comparisons are decided by an order of magnitude, not by a percentage. Asking for more would make this pre-measurement longer than the measurement it exists to unblock.

numbers.name: exposure_time
numbers.note: Given by the person on 2026-09-20 as a STARTING POINT and not a derived optimum, and the difference is the reason this is `assumed:` at E5 rather than anything stronger. No axis produced it and none could -- bounding an exposure needs the brightness this run exists to measure. The commanded value is exactly 0.1 s; the precision is order_of_magnitude because what is known is `about a tenth of a second`, not that tenth to one figure.

numbers.name: illumination_setting
numbers.note: THE PERSON'S 10 PER CENT, AS THE INSTRUMENT TAKES IT: 100, not 10 and not 0.1. Revision 1 wrote `0.1, unit 1` and that was wrong. light_engine_line_intensity_is_per_mille (E3) says each line is two MMCore properties -- `<NAME>` at 0 or 1 and `<NAME>_Intensity` on 0 to 1000 -- so the scale is PER-MILLE and 10 per cent commands 100, while writing 10 would command one per cent. The same tenfold trap is recorded as having already bitten in the prior project, where 5 per cent was written as 50 and 5 would have given 0.5 per cent. The trap is the scale and not the person's number. UNIT `count` IS THE NEAREST LAWFUL ONE AND NOT THE RIGHT ONE. The honest unit is per-mille, which units.json can express -- it is multiplicative, si_factor 0.001, dimensionless, exactly the shape of `mm` for length -- and does not hold. `1` would make this 100 times over rather than a tenth, so `count` is used, the same way nosepiece_position uses it for an index. Raised with manager-microscope. STILL NOT A POWER. There is no calibration from this scale to milliwatts, so writing illumination_power here would assert one nobody has done (kb_gap illumination_dial_to_power).

numbers.name: nosepiece_position
numbers.note: Position 5 is the 100x oil lens; the turret is indexed from 0, which the device table states in its own index_note. `precision` is significant_figures because the enum offers only that and order_of_magnitude: an integer index is exact and the vocabulary has no word for exact, so the nearer of the two is used rather than understating it as an order of magnitude. The grade is E5 because CHOOSING the lens is unevidenced, which is a different thing from the index being exact. Required at all because objective_clearance_min resolves from the objective in the path and refuses without it.

assumptions.statement: A tenth of a second is where the person chose to start. It is not claimed to be right, only to be a place a first frame can be taken from.
assumptions.falsifier: saturated or empty frames in the first record retire it, and this run is the thing that looks

assumptions.statement: Ten per cent of the source's scale is where the person chose to start. The scale is now known to be per-mille, so the commanded value is 100; what stays unevidenced is the choice of ten per cent, not the encoding.
assumptions.falsifier: a first record that is saturated or dark at this setting retires it, and this run is the thing that looks

assumptions.statement: The 100x oil lens, chosen so the result transfers. Brightness is not objective-independent -- collection scales with NA -- so a rate measured at one lens does not carry to another, and the pre-measurement has to be taken at a lens the real measurement is allowed to use. A6 returned four objective-and-zoom pairs that satisfy Nyquist for the diffusivity question and 100x is the only magnification appearing at both zooms, so it is the choice most likely to still be permitted when S4 picks. THAT CARD IS CITED AS A RECORD AND NOT USED AS AN INPUT (4.5.5): no bound here rests on it, and this remains a choice with a falsifier rather than a derived value.
assumptions.falsifier: S4 choosing a pair other than 100x for mic-20260918-001 retires this and the pre-measurement is retaken at the lens it chose

constraint_notes: ONE ACQUISITION, TWO OBSERVABLES, AND THIS CARD DECIDES WHICH WAY. A plan carries one observable, and the two come off one record: the bleaching estimator is the brightness estimator applied frame by frame. So this is ONE plan whose observable is tracer_brightness, with bleaching_rate as a DECLARED BY-PRODUCT of the same record, and not two revisions over one record -- two revisions would imply two acquisitions and this is one. Two result cards come off the one run. The consequence to carry: the record length is set by the BY-PRODUCT rather than by the observable, because brightness is answered in the first frames and a decay constant needs the decay.

The sample is not spent. mic-20260918-001's constraint is that the sample is consumed by the measurement and cannot be remounted; bare particles on a coverslip are NOT that sample -- particles without it. So this pre-measurement does not cost the one mount it exists to protect, and saying so here is the point: without this sentence it reads as if it did.

The single exponential is declared BEFORE the run. bleaching_rate's estimator fixes it, and if the residual says it is wrong THAT IS THE RESULT -- a better-fitting curve is not swapped in afterwards. Stating it on the goal card rather than only in the vocabulary is deliberate: a criterion chosen after the data is not a result, it is a description of the data (5.4).

Both numbers leave as result cards for the librarian (P14) and both carry the illumination setting with them. A bleaching rate without its illumination cannot be used by another plan -- the observable's own note says so -- and the same is true of a brightness. The objective travels with them for the same reason, which the vocabulary does NOT yet say: tracer_brightness's definition names illumination and exposure and not the lens, while collection efficiency scales with NA. Raised with manager-microscope.

Which branch the widefield source sits on is unconfirmed, and this question runs widefield_inline. The registry row says it outright -- role text, `unconfirmed: [branch_assignment]`, `confirmed_by: null`, `gap_ref: lapp_branch_assignment` -- so if source_a is not the inline branch, a run does not know which configuration it is. A configuration is the identity of an optical path and not a label. Carried as a kb_gap and proceeding ON MOCK ONLY: mock moves nothing, so the ambiguity costs nothing until real light. It must be closed before the instrument runs.

THE MASTER STATE IS A CONDITION THIS RUN VERIFIES, and it is the one failure this acquisition is shaped to imitate. `State` at 0 gates the whole engine: no light leaves it however a line and its intensity are set, and NOTHING REPORTS AN ERROR AND BOTH PROPERTIES READ BACK EXACTLY AS WRITTEN (light_engine_master_state_gates_every_line, E3). This run measures brightness and bleaching, and with no light both come out `measured` -- the prior project produced a field whose median was below a dark frame and a ratio computed from hot pixels, and it looked like a result. So the plan carries the master state as a condition the run reads back, and a written-and-read-back property is this defect's SYMPTOM rather than its refutation. 2.1 rule 8 in its sharpest form.

THE PLAN NAMES `LightEngine`, NOT `widefield_source_a`, AND THAT IS WHAT LETS THIS GO BEFORE THE BRANCH GAP CLOSES. getLoadedDevices() returns MMCore labels, so a plan naming `LightEngine` is verified at preflight and asserts nothing about which branch the source sits on. Naming widefield_source_a would assert the disputed mapping -- widefield_inline's own note says a plan that names a source, sets its power or patterns it with the DMD stands on that gap, and setting an intensity is precisely that. MM labels are not product names: `LightEngine` is the Spectra III, `Nosepiece` the Ti2-E. `SpectraIII` fails as device-not-found, which reads as the wrong stand rather than the wrong name.

Exposure and ROI are CORE CALLS and not properties -- setExposure and setROI -- so a preflight looking for them in a device's property list will not find them; only Binning is a property. The turret is the same shape, a state device read with getStateLabel and set with setState, with no Position property (nosepiece_is_an_mmcore_state_device, E3). None of this bites on mock. It is written into the plan now anyway: fixing it when real light arrives is late, and the master-state failure is the kind where the fault looks like a result.

kb_refs.claim: Each light line is two MMCore properties, `<NAME>` at 0 or 1 and `<NAME>_Intensity` on 0 to 1000; the intensity scale is per-mille, so 10 per cent is 100 and 10 is one per cent.
A master property `State` at 0 gates the whole engine: no light leaves it however a line and its intensity are set, and nothing reports an error or reads back wrongly.
The turret is the MMCore label `Nosepiece`, a state device: read with getStateLabel and set with setState, with no Position property.
